title: Federal Register: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Program, final rule (32 CFR part 170)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.
Review correction: clarified the existing-compliance baseline and removed unsupported incremental-cost inference.

publisher: U.S. Department of Defense (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government final rule with regulatory impact analysis
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency is also the party imposing or administering the requirement. Cost figures are the Department's own estimates.
findings: DoD estimates about 1,366,262 contracts and orders per year contain DFARS clause 252.204-7012, going to 31,338 unique awardees; 683,718 awards (50%) go to 23,475 small entities (75% of awardees).
DoD estimates, for a small entity, a Level 2 self-assessment plus initial affirmation costs $34,277 (three-year cost $37,196).
DoD estimates, for a small entity, a Level 2 certification assessment plus initial affirmation costs $101,752 (three-year cost $104,670).
DoD estimates annual Level 1 reaffirmation costs a small entity $560.
The rule states DoD did not count the cost of implementing the security requirements themselves because implementation is already required under existing contract clauses.
limitations: Figures are DoD ex ante estimates from extracted PDF text; table totals were not independently recomputed.

Underlying security-control implementation is excluded because the rule treats it as an existing required/incurred baseline. Exclusion alone does not establish additional remaining or incremental CMMC cost for each contractor; noncompliant firms' remediation is unquantified.
Phase-in dates, the later DFARS acquisition rule and any subsequent changes were not read or verified.
Does not show how many small entities will buy outside help or what they would pay for it.
